source.name: Brevix Fraud Library
source.description: Curated small-business fraud investigation playbooks maintained by Brevix. Symptoms are written in owner language so natural-language concerns match lexically.

playbooks.title: Duplicate invoice and split payment review
playbooks.description: Investigate repeated vendor invoices, invoices paid twice, and payments split below approval thresholds.
symptoms: an invoice was paid twice
we got double charged by a vendor
the same bill shows up more than once
duplicate payments to one vendor in the same week
red_flags: duplicate invoice numbers or amounts to the same vendor
multiple payments just below an approval threshold
invoice numbers that increment suspiciously fast
same invoice paid from two different accounts
tests: match invoice numbers against vendor and payment date
group payments by vendor and amount within 30-day windows
compare split payments against the approval threshold
document_requests: bank statements for the affected months

playbooks.title: Ghost employee payroll review
playbooks.description: Investigate payroll payments to employees with missing HR records, unknown names, or shared deposit accounts.
symptoms: there is an employee on payroll I don't recognize
someone on the payroll never shows up to work
payroll headcount doesn't match the people I employ
a terminated employee is still being paid
red_flags: employee has no personnel file or tax forms
two employees share a bank account or address
no time entries but regular paychecks
pay continues after termination date
tests: reconcile payroll register against HR records and tax filings
match employee deposit accounts for duplicates
compare time entries to paychecks per employee

playbooks.title: Related party supplier review
playbooks.description: Review vendor master data for hidden relationships between vendors and employees.
symptoms: a vendor and an employee might be connected
same bank account shared by employee and vendor
vendor address looks like an employee's home address
red_flags: vendor bank account matches an employee direct deposit account
shared home address between vendor and employee
vendor registered shortly before first large payment
employee approves invoices for a vendor they created
tests: compare vendor bank accounts to employee direct deposit accounts
match vendor addresses and phone numbers against employee records
review who created and who approves each vendor

playbooks.title: Shell vendor and fictitious billing review
playbooks.description: Investigate vendors that may not exist: no services delivered, vague invoices, and payments to entities with no footprint.
symptoms: we are paying a vendor no one remembers hiring
invoices are vague and don't say what we bought
I can't find any information about this supplier
red_flags: vendor has no website, phone, or physical address
invoices lack detail, PO references, or receiving records
payments started without a contract or onboarding
vendor name is similar to a real supplier but not identical
tests: verify vendor registration and tax identifiers
trace three invoices to goods received or services delivered
compare vendor names for near-duplicates of legitimate suppliers

playbooks.title: Payment redirection and vendor email compromise review
playbooks.description: Investigate changed remittance details, urgent wire requests, and email-initiated banking changes (business email compromise).
symptoms: a vendor says they never received our payment
we got an email asking to change bank details
money was wired to the wrong account
someone impersonated our CEO or a supplier by email
red_flags: bank detail change requested by email shortly before a large payment
reply-to domain differs subtly from the vendor's real domain
urgency and secrecy pressure in payment requests
remittance account in a different country or name
tests: verify every recent bank-detail change by phone against a known number
compare remittance accounts before and after the change request
review email headers for spoofed or lookalike domains
document_requests: bank change request emails with full headers

playbooks.title: Payroll spike and off-cycle payment review
playbooks.description: Investigate sudden payroll increases, off-cycle runs, unapproved bonuses, and rate changes.
symptoms: payroll jumped this month and I don't know why
there was an extra payroll run I didn't approve
someone's pay rate changed without authorization
overtime is way higher than normal
red_flags: off-cycle payroll runs without documented approval
rate changes entered and approved by the same person
bonuses outside the normal review period
overtime concentrated on one employee or approver
tests: compare payroll totals month over month by employee
list off-cycle runs and match each to an approval
review rate-change audit history for self-approval
document_requests: payroll registers for the last six months

playbooks.title: Bookkeeper transition and segregation of duties review
playbooks.description: Review control exposure when one person controls the books — especially after a bookkeeper quits, is terminated, or refuses to share access.
symptoms: my bookkeeper quit suddenly
one person controls both payments and reconciliation
the bookkeeper won't let anyone else see the books
records are missing after a staff change
red_flags: same person initiates payments and reconciles the bank
reconciliations are late, missing, or done only by one person
the departing bookkeeper deleted or exported records
vendors or balances changed right before the departure
tests: inventory who can initiate, approve, and reconcile payments
re-perform the last three bank reconciliations independently
review audit logs around the transition date
document_requests: bank reconciliations for the last six months
accounting system access and audit logs
list of open vendor and payroll changes in the transition window

playbooks.title: IRS notice and payroll tax diversion review
playbooks.description: Investigate IRS balance-due or missing-deposit notices that may indicate withheld payroll taxes were diverted rather than deposited.
symptoms: we got an IRS notice saying we owe payroll taxes
the IRS says deposits are missing but we recorded them
a CP504 or levy notice arrived unexpectedly
our payroll company says taxes were paid but the IRS disagrees
red_flags: recorded tax deposits with no matching bank withdrawal
941 filings that don't reconcile to payroll registers
notices intercepted or hidden from the owner
payroll tax payments routed through a personal or unknown account
tests: reconcile 941 filings to payroll registers and bank withdrawals
obtain IRS account transcripts and compare to the ledger
verify deposit destinations for payroll tax payments
document_requests: payroll tax ledger entries and bank statements

playbooks.title: Vendor concentration and kickback indicators review
playbooks.description: Review unusually concentrated vendor spend and buyer favoritism that can indicate kickbacks or conflicts of interest.
symptoms: one vendor gets most of our money
prices from a favored supplier keep going up
an employee always pushes the same vendor
we never get competitive bids
red_flags: single vendor share of category spend above 60 percent
sole-source awards without documented justification
price increases above market without renegotiation
buyer lifestyle changes or gifts from the vendor
tests: rank vendor spend concentration by category
compare unit prices against alternative suppliers
review bid records for the top vendors

playbooks.title: Expense reimbursement abuse review
playbooks.description: Investigate inflated, duplicated, personal, or fictitious employee expense claims.
symptoms: expense reports look inflated
the same receipt was submitted twice
personal purchases are showing up as business expenses
one employee's expenses are far above everyone else's
red_flags: duplicate receipts across reports or employees
round-dollar claims just under receipt-required limits
weekend or vacation-period business expenses
merchant categories inconsistent with job role
tests: match receipts across reports for duplicates
compare claim amounts to policy thresholds
rank expense totals by employee against peers

playbooks.title: Check tampering and signature review
playbooks.description: Investigate altered payees, forged signatures, out-of-sequence checks, and checks written to unexpected parties.
symptoms: a check was altered or the payee looks changed
checks are missing from the checkbook
cleared checks don't match the register
a check was cashed that I never signed
red_flags: payee on the cleared check differs from the register
out-of-sequence or voided-then-cleared checks
signatures that don't match authorized signers
checks payable to employees, cash, or unknown parties
tests: compare cleared check images to the check register
list gaps and voids in check sequences
verify signatures on large checks against authorized signers
document_requests: cleared check images from the bank

playbooks.title: Cash skimming and unrecorded sales review
playbooks.description: Investigate cash that disappears before it is recorded: register shortages, missing deposits, and declining cash ratios.
symptoms: cash is missing from the register
deposits are smaller than daily sales
cash sales are down but card sales are steady
money seems to disappear before it hits the bank
red_flags: deposit totals routinely below point-of-sale cash totals
no-sale and void transactions clustered on one shift
declining cash-to-card ratio without a business reason
deposits made days after the sales date
tests: reconcile daily POS cash totals to bank deposits
trend cash-to-card ratio by month and by shift
review void and no-sale activity by employee

playbooks.title: Approval threshold evasion and round-dollar review
playbooks.description: Review payments engineered to dodge approval limits: split purchases, round-dollar patterns, and just-below-threshold clustering.
symptoms: lots of payments just under our approval limit
purchases keep getting split into smaller pieces
too many perfectly round payment amounts
red_flags: clusters of payments within 5 percent below the approval threshold
sequential same-day purchases from one vendor
high frequency of round-dollar amounts versus peers
tests: histogram payment amounts around approval thresholds
group same-vendor same-day payments and sum them
measure round-dollar frequency by vendor and requester
document_requests: payment listing with requester and approver

playbooks.title: Company card misuse review
playbooks.description: Investigate personal or unauthorized spending on company credit and debit cards.
symptoms: personal charges are showing up on the company card
there are subscriptions on the card nobody recognizes
card spending doubled with no new business activity
cash advances on the company card
red_flags: merchants inconsistent with business needs (retail, travel, gaming)
recurring subscriptions with no assigned owner
cash advances or gift card purchases
charges on weekends, holidays, or during leave
tests: categorize card merchants and flag personal-category spend
list recurring charges and confirm business owners for each
compare card activity against work schedules
document_requests: card statements for the last six months

playbooks.title: Refund and credit memo abuse review
playbooks.description: Investigate fictitious refunds and credit memos used to pocket cash or conceal theft.
symptoms: refunds are way up but returns aren't
credit memos keep getting issued to the same customer
a refund went to a card or account that never purchased anything
red_flags: refunds without matching original sales
credit memos concentrated on one employee's logins
refunds to payment methods different from the original sale
refund spikes on specific shifts
tests: match each refund to an original transaction
rank refund and credit volume by employee
compare refund payment destinations to original tender
document_requests: original sales records for refunded items
